questions.text: समग्र माँग में किसी भी प्रकार की कमी को हतोत्साहित करने के लिए भारत सरकार _______ में _______ कर सकती है ।
questions.text_english: In order to discourage any fall in Aggregate Demand, the Government of India may _______ the _______.
questions.instruction_line: (रिक्त स्थानों को भरने के लिए सही विकल्प का चयन कीजिए)
questions.instruction_line_english: (Choose the correct alternative to fill in the blanks)
questions.solution: Correct option is D. To prevent a fall in Aggregate Demand, the government should increase demand. Reducing tax rates increases disposable income for households, leading to higher consumption and thus higher Aggregate Demand. Other options like decreasing government expenditure would further reduce Aggregate Demand.

questions.text_english:
Choose the correct alternative to complete the given schedule :

Round | Deposits | Loans (90%) | Reserve Ratio (10%)
I | 2000 | 1800 | 200
II | ...(i)... | ...(ii)... | 180
Total | ...(iii) | ...(iv) | 2000
questions.solution: Correct option is D. In the credit creation process, the loans of the previous round become the deposits of the next round. Thus, (i) = 1800. Then, 90% of 1800 = 1620 (ii). Total deposits = Initial deposit / LRR = 2000 / 0.10 = 20000 (iii). Total loans = Total deposits - Total reserves = 20000 - 2000 = 18000 (iv).

questions.instruction_line: दिए गए कथनों के आलोक में, निम्नलिखित में से सही विकल्प का चयन कीजिए :

options_english.A: Statement 1 is true and Statement 2 is false.

questions.solution: Correct option is A. Statement 1 is true because constant MPC leads to a linear consumption function. questions.text: निम्नलिखित कथनों को पढ़िए: अभिकथन (A) और कारण (R) । अभिकथन (A) : प्रतिकूल व्यापार संतुलन की स्थिति में, एक राष्ट्र का चालू खाता अधिशेष में हो सकता है । कारण (R) : किसी राष्ट्र की निवल अदृश्य प्राप्तियाँ, निवल दृश्य प्राप्तियों से अधिक हो सकती हैं ।

questions.instruction_line: नीचे दिए गए विकल्पों में से सही विकल्प का चयन कीजिए :
questions.instruction_line_english: Choose the correct alternative from those given below :

options.A: अभिकथन (A) और कारण (R) दोनों सत्य हैं और कारण (R), अभिकथन (A) की सही व्याख्या करता है ।
options.B: अभिकथन (A) और कारण (R) दोनों सत्य हैं, लेकिन कारण (R), अभिकथन (A) की सही व्याख्या नहीं करता है ।
options.C: अभिकथन (A) सत्य है, लेकिन कारण (R) असत्य है ।
options.D: अभिकथन (A) असत्य है, लेकिन कारण (R) सत्य है ।

options_english.A: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of the Assertion (A).
options_english.B: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of the Assertion (A).
options_english.C: Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.
options_english.D: Assertion (A) is false, but Reason (R) is true.

questions.solution: Correct option is A. An unfavourable Balance of Trade means imports of goods exceed exports (negative visible balance). However, the Current Account includes both visible and invisible trade. If net invisible receipts are large enough to cover the negative visible balance, the Current Account can still show a surplus.

questions.text: पहचानिए कि एक अर्थव्यवस्था के संदर्भ में निम्नलिखित में से कौन-सा कथन असत्य है ।

options.A: सकल राष्ट्रीय उत्पाद (GNP) की सकल घरेलू उत्पाद (GDP) पर अधिकता संभव है।
options.B: सकल घरेलू उत्पाद (GDP) की सकल राष्ट्रीय उत्पाद (GNP) पर अधिकता संभव है।
options.C: सकल राष्ट्रीय उत्पाद (GNP) तथा सकल घरेलू उत्पाद (GDP) में समानता संभव है।
options.D: सकल राष्ट्रीय उत्पाद (GNP) तथा सकल घरेलू उत्पाद (GDP) का योग सदैव शून्य (0) के बराबर होता है ।

options_english.A: Excess of Gross National Product (GNP) over Gross Domestic Product (GDP) is possible.
options_english.B: Excess of Gross Domestic Product (GDP) over Gross National Product (GNP) is possible.
options_english.C: Equality between Gross National Product (GNP) and Gross Domestic Product (GDP) is possible.
options_english.D: Sum of Gross National Product (GNP) and Gross Domestic Product (GDP) is always equal to zero (0).

questions.solution: Correct option is D. Statements A, B, and C are possible depending on Net Factor Income from Abroad (NFIA). Statement D is mathematically incorrect as there is no economic theory stating that the sum of GDP and GNP must be zero.

questions.solution: Correct option is C. Credit Multiplier = 1/LRR. Therefore, an inverse relationship exists between the reserve ratio and credit creation (Statement 1 true). The Central Bank controls this process via monetary policy instruments (Statement 2 true).

questions.text:
(क) दिए गए आँकड़ों के आधार पर, राष्ट्रीय आय के मूल्य का आकलन कीजिए :

(i) सरकारी अंतिम उपभोग व्यय : 110
(ii) निजी अंतिम उपभोग व्यय : 200
(iii) सकल घरेलू स्थिर पूँजी निर्माण : 30
(iv) निवल निर्यात : (-) 40
(v) स्टॉक में वृद्धि : 20
(vi) स्थायी पूँजी का उपभोग : 15
(vii) अप्रत्यक्ष कर : 60
(viii) उपदान : 15
(ix) विदेशों से प्राप्त शुद्ध कारक आय : 40
questions.text_english:
(a) On the basis of the given data, estimate the value of National Income:

(i) Government Final Consumption Expenditure : 110
(ii) Private Final Consumption Expenditure : 200
(iii) Gross Domestic Fixed Capital Formation : 30
(iv) Net Exports : (-) 40
(v) Increase in Stock : 20
(vi) Consumption of Fixed Capital : 15
(vii) Indirect Taxes : 60
(viii) Subsidies : 15
(ix) Net Factor Income from Abroad : 40

key_points: GDP_MP = Private Final Consumption Expenditure + Government Final Consumption Expenditure + Gross Domestic Fixed Capital Formation + Increase in Stock + Net Exports
NNP_FC (National Income) = GDP_MP - Consumption of Fixed Capital - Indirect Taxes + Subsidies + NFIA
National Income = 320 - 15 - 60 + 15 + 40 = 300

questions.solution: To calculate National Income, we first determine GDP at Market Price using the expenditure method. GDP_MP is the sum of Private Final Consumption Expenditure (200), Government Final Consumption Expenditure (110), Gross Domestic Fixed Capital Formation (30), Increase in Stock (20), and Net Exports (-40), which equals 320 crore. To reach National Income (NNP at Factor Cost), we subtract consumption of fixed capital (15), subtract net indirect taxes (60 - 15 = 45), and add net factor income from abroad (40). Thus, National Income = 320 - 15 - 45 + 40 = 300 crore.

questions.text: किसी राष्ट्र की विदेशी मुद्रा की माँग को प्रत्यक्ष रूप से प्रभावित करने वाले किन्हीं दो कारकों की विवेचना कीजिए ।
questions.text_english: Discuss any two factors which directly affect the demand for foreign exchange of a nation.

key_points: Import of goods and services: When a country imports goods/services, it needs foreign currency to make payments, increasing demand.
Investment in foreign countries: When domestic residents invest in assets or financial instruments abroad, it leads to a demand for foreign currency.

questions.solution: The two primary factors affecting the demand for foreign exchange are imports and foreign investments. First, when a nation imports goods and services from abroad, domestic importers must pay in foreign currency, which creates a demand for that currency in the foreign exchange market. Second, when domestic residents seek to invest in foreign assets, real estate, or stocks, they must convert domestic currency into foreign currency, thereby increasing the demand for foreign exchange.

questions.text: (क) एक काल्पनिक अर्थव्यवस्था के लिए, सरकार ₹ 5,000 करोड़ का अतिरिक्त निवेश व्यय करती है । यह मानते हुए कि सीमांत बचत प्रवृत्ति (MPS) अपने 20% के वर्तमान स्तर से आधी हो गई है, सीमांत बचत प्रवृत्ति (MPS) में इस गिरावट के कारण आय में परिवर्तन का अनुमान लगाइए । (ख) स्वायत्त निवेश का अर्थ लिखिए ।
questions.text_english: (a) For a hypothetical economy, the government incurs an additional investment expenditure of ₹ 5,000 crore. Assuming that the Marginal Propensity to Save (MPS) becomes half from its present level of 20%, estimate the change in income due to this fall in Marginal Propensity to Save (MPS). (b) State the meaning of autonomous investment.

sub_questions.text: निवेश गुणांक की गणना और आय में परिवर्तन ।
sub_questions.text_english: Calculation of Investment Multiplier and change in Income.

key_points: Old MPS = 0.20, New MPS = 0.10
New Multiplier (k) = 1/MPS = 1/0.10 = 10
Change in Income (ΔY) = k * ΔI = 10 * 5000 = 50,000 crore

sub_questions.solution: Given the initial MPS is 20% (0.20), it becomes half, making the new MPS 10% (0.10). The investment multiplier (k) is calculated as 1/MPS, which equals 1/0.10 = 10. The change in income (ΔY) is the multiplier (k) multiplied by the change in investment (ΔI). Therefore, ΔY = 10 * 5,000 = 50,000 crore.

key_points: Investment independent of income level.

sub_questions.solution: Autonomous investment refers to investment expenditure that is independent of the level of income or profit in the economy. It is usually determined by factors like technology or government policy.

questions.text: किसी द्वि-क्षेत्रक अर्थव्यवस्था में समग्र पूर्ति के दो घटकों की विस्तार से व्याख्या कीजिए ।
questions.text_english: Elaborate the two components of Aggregate Supply in a two-sector economy.

key_points: Aggregate Supply is the total output of goods and services planned to be produced.
Component 1: Consumption (C) - part of income spent.
Component 2: Savings (S) - part of income not spent.

questions.solution: In a two-sector economy (comprising households and firms), Aggregate Supply (AS) is represented by total national income (Y). Since income is either spent on consumption (C) or saved (S), AS is defined by the identity Y = C + S. Consumption refers to the expenditure by households on goods and services for satisfaction, while Savings represents the portion of income that is not consumed. Both C and S are essential components that together constitute the total flow of income or Aggregate Supply.

questions.text:
(क) "भारतीय रिज़र्व बैंक (RBI) द्वारा खुले बाज़ार में संचालन (Open Market Operations) अर्थव्यवस्था में मुद्रा आपूर्ति को विनियमित करने में सहायता करते हैं।" मान्य तर्कों सहित दिए गए कथन को सिद्ध कीजिए।
अथवा
(ख) किसी राष्ट्र के केन्द्रीय बैंक के 'बैंकों के बैंक' कार्य की विस्तार से व्याख्या कीजिए।
questions.text_english:
(a) "Open market operations by the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) help in regulating money supply in the economy." Justify the given statement with valid arguments.
OR
(b) Elaborate the 'Bankers' Bank' function of the Central Bank of a nation.

key_points: OMO involves buying/selling government securities.
Buying securities increases money supply by injecting liquidity into the market.
Selling securities decreases money supply by absorbing liquidity from the market.

questions.solution: Open market operations (OMO) are a vital tool of monetary policy. When the RBI wants to increase the money supply, it purchases government securities from the open market, injecting cash into the economy. Conversely, to reduce the money supply, the RBI sells these securities, which drains cash from the banking system, thereby restricting the lending capacity of commercial banks and controlling inflation.

questions.text:
(क) (i) एक द्वि-क्षेत्रक अर्थव्यवस्था में आय के चक्रीय प्रवाह की अवधारणा की व्याख्या कीजिए।
(ii) "किसी अर्थव्यवस्था में सकल घरेलू उत्पाद (GDP) व सकल मूल्य वर्धित (GVA) का योग सदैव बराबर होते हैं।" मान्य तर्कों सहित दिए गए कथन को सिद्ध कीजिए।

(ख) (i) "सकल घरेलू उत्पाद (GDP) अवस्फीतिक वास्तविक GDP व मौद्रिक GDP के अनुपात द्वारा दर्शाया जाता है।" क्या आप दिए गए कथन से सहमत हैं? एक काल्पनिक संख्यात्मक उदाहरण व मान्य तर्कों द्वारा अपने उत्तर की पुष्टि कीजिए।

key_points: Statement is false.
Deflator = Nominal GDP / Real GDP * 100.

questions.text_english:
(a) On the basis of the given information, calculate the values of the following: (i) Fiscal Deficit (ii) Primary Deficit
(i) Capital Expenditure : 60
(ii) Revenue Receipts : 50
(iii) Revenue Deficit : 55
(iv) Interest Payments : 20
(v) Non-Debt Creating Capital Receipts : 50% of Revenue Receipts = 25
(b) State any two examples of public goods. (c) Distinguish between 'Public Provision' and 'Public Production'.

key_points: Total Expenditure - Total Receipts (excluding borrowings)
Fiscal Deficit = Revenue Deficit + Capital Expenditure - Non-Debt Creating Capital Receipts

sub_questions.solution: Fiscal Deficit is calculated as (Revenue Expenditure - Revenue Receipts) + (Capital Expenditure - Non-Debt Creating Capital Receipts). Given Revenue Deficit (Revenue Expenditure - Revenue Receipts) is 55, Capital Expenditure is 60, and Non-Debt Creating Capital Receipts are 25, the Fiscal Deficit = 55 + 60 - 25 = 90 crore.

key_points: Primary Deficit = Fiscal Deficit - Interest Payments

sub_questions.solution: Primary Deficit is the Fiscal Deficit minus Interest Payments. Using the result from the previous calculation (90) and interest payments (20), Primary Deficit = 90 - 20 = 70 crore.

key_points: National defence, public parks.

sub_questions.text_english: Difference between Public Provision and Public Production

key_points: Provision: Government finances the good.
Production: Government produces the good.

sub_questions.solution: Public provision means the government provides the good free of cost or at a subsidized rate, often financed through taxes. Public production means the government itself produces the good (e.g., through a public enterprise). Both may coexist, but one refers to financing and the other to the actual manufacturing or delivery.

questions.text_english: (a) Discuss any two salient features of Indian industrial sector during the period of 1950 - 1990. OR (b) Describe any two purposes for the founding of World Trade Organisation (WTO) in 1995.

key_points: Feature 1: Protection through import substitution (high tariffs and quotas).
Feature 2: Dominance of Public Sector Enterprises (PSUs) in key industries.

questions.solution: Two salient features of the Indian industrial sector during 1950-1990 were, first, the protection of domestic industries from foreign competition through high import tariffs and strict quotas (Import Substitution). Second, the government emphasized the role of the public sector, with public sector enterprises being given the central role in major industrial activities, while the private sector was subject to strict regulation.

questions.text: दिए गए आँकड़ों से, सकल मूल्य वर्धित (GVA) में भारत व चीन के क्षेत्रीय योगदान की तुलना व विश्लेषण कीजिए ।
questions.text_english: From the given data, compare and analyse India and China's sectoral contribution towards Gross Value Added (GVA).
questions.instruction_line: 2018-2019 में रोज़गार एवं सकल मूल्य वर्धित (%) के क्षेत्र शेयर (तालिका दी गई है)
questions.instruction_line_english: Sectoral Share of Employment and GVA (%) in 2018-2019 (Table provided)

key_points: Agriculture GVA: India (16%) > China (7%).
Industry GVA: China (41%) > India (30%).
Services GVA: India (54%) and China (52%) are comparable.

questions.solution: The analysis shows that India relies more on the agricultural sector for GVA (16%) compared to China (7%), indicating China's shift towards industrialization. China's industrial sector contributes significantly more (41%) to its GVA than India's (30%), reflecting China's focus as the 'factory of the world'. In the services sector, both nations have a similar contribution, with India at 54% and China at 52%, showing that both have successfully transitioned towards a service-oriented economy.

questions.text: चित्र में दर्शाई गई परिस्थिति की पहचान कीजिए तथा भारतीय अर्थव्यवस्था पर संकेतित स्थिति के प्रभाव का सुझाव दीजिए ।
questions.text_english: Identify the situation depicted in the image and suggest the impact of the indicated situation in the Indian economy.

key_points: Image shows street/informal vending.
Informal sector impact: lack of job security, no social protection, low income.
Need for formalization.

questions.solution: The image depicts street vendors or workers in the informal sector, common in developing economies like India. The informal sector is characterized by low productivity, lack of job security, absence of social protection (like health insurance or pensions), and uncertain incomes. In the Indian economy, this leads to a 'working poor' class, widening income inequality, and limits the government's ability to tax or regulate, thus hindering sustainable economic development.

(a) (i) "India's inward looking trade policy during the post-independence period was well supported by various tariff and non-tariff barriers." Do you agree with the given statement? Justify your answer with valid arguments.
(ii) "Navratna policy has facilitated the maintenance, promotion and disinvestment of Public Sector Undertakings (PSUs)." Justify the given statement with valid explanation.
OR

key_points: Agree: High tariffs discouraged imports to protect domestic industry.
Quotas limited quantity of imports.

sub_questions.solution: Yes, I agree. Post-independence, India followed an inward-looking policy, often called import substitution. The government imposed high tariff barriers on imported goods and quantitative quotas to limit imports. This was done to shield nascent domestic industries from competition, allow them time to develop, and achieve self-reliance.

key_points: Navratna status gives autonomy for efficient management.
Improved performance facilitates potential disinvestment.

sub_questions.solution: The Navratna policy granted operational and managerial autonomy to high-performing PSUs. By providing this autonomy, the government enabled these companies to operate more efficiently in a competitive market. Improved performance and professional management not only helped maintain these enterprises but also made them attractive for disinvestment, as they became more profitable and better positioned for private participation.

समकालीन विश्व में जहाँ सतत विकास को लेकर बहुत सारी चिंताएँ हैं, हरित विकास तथा शुद्ध शून्य उत्सर्जन ऐसी दो महत्त्वपूर्ण अवधारणाएँ हैं जिनकी आमतौर पर एक साथ चर्चा की जाती है। ये दो अवधारणाएँ पृथ्वी के भविष्य के लिए अतिसंवेदनशील हैं, क्योंकि इन पर एक साथ काम करके, हम अपने लिए तथा आने वाली पीढ़ियों के लिए एक अधिक स्थायी भविष्य का निर्माण कर सकते हैं।

हरित विकास उस आर्थिक विकास को संदर्भित करता है "जो पर्यावरणीय प्रभाव को कम करने के तरीके से हासिल किया गया है," जबकि, "शुद्ध शून्य उत्सर्जन ग्रीनहाउस गैसों के मानवजनित उत्सर्जन व वायुमंडल से ऐसे उत्सर्जन को हटाने के बीच संतुलन प्राप्त करने की स्थिति है।"

दोनों अवधारणाओं के बीच एक मजबूत संबंध मौजूद है :
(1) हरित विकास ग्रीनहाउस गैस उत्सर्जन को कम करने में सहायक है, जो शुद्ध शून्य उत्सर्जन प्राप्त करने के लिए आवश्यक है।
(2) हरित विकास नौकरियाँ उत्पन्न करने में व आर्थिक विकास को प्रोत्साहित करने में सहायक है, जो देशों के लिए शुद्ध शून्य उत्सर्जन प्रौद्योगिकी में निवेश को अधिक किफायती बनाने में सहायता कर सकता है।

एक राष्ट्र इन दोनों कारकों को एक साथ वृद्धि देने के लिए बहुत कुछ कर सकता है, जैसे :
(क) नवीकरणीय ऊर्जा स्रोतों में निवेश, जो ग्रीनहाउस गैसों का उत्पादन नहीं करते हैं।
(ख) ऊर्जा कुशल उपायों को अपनाना जैसे इन्सुलेशन और अन्य ऐसे उपकरण जो ऊर्जा की खपत को कम करने में मदद कर सकते हैं।
(ग) परिवहन की आदतों में परिवर्तन जैसे पैदल चलना, साइकिल चलाना व सार्वजनिक परिवहन का उपयोग करना, क्योंकि ये यात्रा करने के लिए अल्प-कार्बन उत्सर्जन वाले तरीके हैं।
questions.text_english:
In the contemporary world with a lot of sustainable development concerns, green growth and net zero emissions are two important concepts which are generally discussed together. These two concepts are essential for the future of the Earth, as by working together on them we can create a more sustainable future for ourselves and for the generations to come.

Green growth refers to, "the economic growth that is achieved in a way that minimizes environmental impact," whereas, "net zero emission is the state of achieving balance between anthropogenic emission of greenhouse gases and removal of such emissions from the atmosphere."

There exists a robust connection between the two concepts:
(1) Green growth can help to reduce greenhouse gas emissions, which is essential for achieving net zero emissions.
(2) Green growth can help to create jobs and boost economic growth, which can help to make it more affordable for countries to invest in net zero emissions technology.

A nation can do a lot to promote these two factors together, like:
(a) Investing in renewable energy sources which do not produce greenhouse gases.
(b) Adopting energy efficient measures, such as insulation and other such appliances which can help to reduce energy consumption.
(c) Altering transportation habits, like adopting walking, biking and using public transportation as they are lower-carbon ways to travel.

sub_questions.text_english: State the meaning of green growth and net zero emissions.

key_points: Green growth: Economic growth minimizing environmental impact.
Net zero: Balance between greenhouse gas emission and removal.

sub_questions.solution: As stated in the passage, green growth refers to economic growth achieved by minimizing environmental impact. Net zero emission is the state where a balance is achieved between human-made greenhouse gas emissions and the removal of such gases from the atmosphere.

sub_questions.text: हरित विकास और शुद्ध शून्य उत्सर्जन के बीच अंतर्संबंध पर संक्षेप में चर्चा कीजिए ।
sub_questions.text_english: Discuss briefly the interconnection between green growth and net zero emissions.

key_points: Green growth reduces emissions (essential for Net Zero).
Green growth provides economic means/jobs to invest in net zero technology.

sub_questions.solution: The passage identifies a robust connection: first, green growth directly helps reduce greenhouse gas emissions, which is a prerequisite for reaching net zero status. Second, green growth boosts the economy and creates jobs, providing the necessary financial capacity for nations to invest in the advanced technology required for net zero emissions.

sub_questions.text: शुद्ध शून्य उत्सर्जन को प्रोत्साहित करने वाले किसी एक कारक को सोदाहरण स्पष्ट कीजिए ।
sub_questions.text_english: Illustrate any one factor to promote net zero emission.

key_points: Example: Investment in renewable energy (e.g., solar or wind power).

sub_questions.solution: One effective factor is investing in renewable energy sources. For instance, shifting from coal-based power generation to solar or wind power drastically reduces greenhouse gas emissions, directly contributing to the goal of achieving net zero emissions.
